extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of mathematics and classical mechanics (readers of Newton/Principia)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the principal lemmas, propositions, experimental methods, and methodological rules from a classical mechanics mathematical treatise (Newtonian lemmas and Proposition I on centripetal forces). Includes limit-method principles, collision/pendulum experimental procedure, and geometric lemmas about curves and areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of quantity of motion in collisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A congressu & collisione corporum nunquam mutabatur quantitas motus (The quantity of motion is never changed by the collision/concourse of bodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained with pendulum collision experiments: measured changes in parts of motion transferred from one body to another (examples with numbers: A striking B with nine parts transfers seven etc.), and procedure notes on measurement errors (digit-level accuracy) and experimental difficulties (unequal densities, textures). Use repeated pendulum experiments at different lengths and masses to observe that action and reaction give equal changes in motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action and reaction equality (Third Law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut actionem & reactionem semper esse sequales (Action and reaction are always equal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argued from pendulum/congress experiments and extended to machines and moving instruments: action & reaction in all usages of instruments are mutually equal; when action propagates through an instrument and is finally impressed on a resisting body, its final determination is contrary to the determination of the reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for correcting pendulum experiments for air resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: use chords of arcs to deduce velocities just before and after reflection, locate points to correct measured maxima for the effect of air resistance, and thereby obtain the motion 'as if in vacuum'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed stepwise experimental method: suspend spherical bodies, draw semicircles about centers, displace one body to a point R, release (with the other removed) and measure the point V to which it returns after one oscillation. Define intermediate points S,T (quarters) so chords TF and others equalize; use chord TA to represent velocity proximate prior to reflection and chord tA proximate after reflection. Repeat for both bodies and compare motions to obtain corrected velocities and verify equality of action/reaction. Notes caution about imperfect elasticity, unequal densities, textural irregularities, and digit measurement errors; suggests using long pendula (8-16 feet) and many trials to reduce error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elasticity and returned velocity rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In theoretic perfectly elastic bodies return with the incident velocity; in imperfectly elastic bodies the return velocity is diminished in proportion to the elastic force present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental observations: tightly conglomerated wool spheres returned with relative velocity approximations ~5:9; steel similar; cork somewhat smaller; glass ~15:16. Procedure: first measure reflection of pendula to determine elastic force magnitude; then determine reflections in various collision cases using that force. Caveat: elasticity may cause part damage or extension (malleation) altering outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutuality of attraction (gravitation/other attractions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In attractiones rem sic breviter ostendo: corporibus duobus mutuo trahentibus ... praesuppono obstaculum interponi — resulting argument shows the attractions are mutual and equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thought experiment/experiment: place obstacle between two mutually attracting bodies; pressure distribution shows neither body will displace the other preferentially without contradiction to earlier laws. Practical trial with magnet and iron: when separated and floated in water they remain stationary relative to each other, sustaining mutual attractions and eventually resting in equilibrium. Extended to gravity between Earth and its parts to show mutual equal tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machines: velocity–force reciprocity and efficiency principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In instrumentis aptis vis efficacia consistit in diminuendo velocitatem augeamus vim, & contra: if velocities of agent and resisted are reciprocals of forces, the agent sustains the resistance; by decreasing velocity one increases force and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General mechanical principle: given a weight and a driving force, machines are formed so that agent and resistent velocities are reciprocals to their forces. If velocity disparity is large enough to overcome all resistances (friction, cohesion, lifting resistances), surplus force produces acceleration. Examples include levers, pulleys (trochlea/polyspasto), screw/handle relations, wedge (cuneus) relations, and handles/cochlea: circular velocity of handle relates to progressive velocity of screw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for method of ultimate ratios (limits) over indivisibles
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodo evanescentium summas & rationes, primasque nascentium, id est ad limites summarum & rationum deducere — demonstrations are reduced to limits of sums and ratios (ultimate ratios) rather than indivisibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanatory scholium defends use of limits (ultimae rationes) to avoid the perceived hardness/less geometric nature of indivisibles; describes meaning of 'ultimate' quantities (the value at the instant of vanishing or arising) and addresses objections (e.g., that evanescent quantities have no ultima ratio) by clarifying limits are the definite bounds quantities approach without transgressing. Advises reading quantities 'as small as one pleases' (diminishing without bound).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma I — ultimate equality of quantities whose ratios approach equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitates, ut & quantitatum rationes, quce ad cequalitatem tempore quovis finito constanter tendunt ... fiunt ultimo ceqtiales (If ratios of quantities constantly tend to equality before the end of a finite time, they are ultimately equal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: assuming ultimate inequality yields impossibility of approaching equality beyond a given difference. This lemma underpins reasoning about limits/ultimate ratios throughout the treatise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma II — inscribed and circumscribed parallelogram approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a curve with bounding straight lines has repeated inscribed parallelograms of equal bases and with widths diminished to infinity, then the ultimate ratios of sums of the parallelograms coincide with the curvilinear figure (inscribed and circumscribed figures become ultimately equal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct sequences of parallelograms under the curve whose widths shrink; their sums differ from the figure by a rectangle whose width can be made less than any given quantity; thus by Lemma I their ultimate ratios coincide. Corollaries: rectilinear figures composed of vanishing chords converge to the curved figure; circumscribed rectilinear figure with tangents likewise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma III — unequal latitudes but same limit result
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the parallelograms' latitudes (widths) are unequal but each is diminished to infinity, the ultimate ratios of inscribed vs circumscribed remain equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take maximum latitude and construct parallelogram exceeding the difference; as maximum latitude is decreased to infinity the excess becomes arbitrarily small; apply Lemma I to conclude equality in the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma IV — correspondence of ultimate ratios for two figures subdivided equally
rubrics_metrics.description: If two figures are each inscribed by the same number of parallelogram-series with latitudes diminished to infinity, and the ultimate ratios of corresponding parallelograms are given, then the two figures themselves are in that same ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: summing corresponding parallelograms gives sums in the same ratio, hence figures are in same ratio (corollary: applies to any two quantities divided into arbitrarily many parts — totals inherit the ultimate ratio of parts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma V — proportionality of corresponding sides and areas for similar figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Similium figurarum latera omnia ... sunt proportionalia, tam curvilinea quam rectilinea; & areæ sunt in duplicata ratione laterum (All corresponding sides of similar figures, curvilinear or rectilinear, are proportional; areas are in the duplicate ratio of sides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard similarity property extended to curvilinear figures via the method of limits. Use when comparing areas and linear measures in limit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma VI — chord–tangent angle vanishes as points coalesce
rubrics_metrics.description: If any arc subtends chord AB and at a point A the curve is continuously curved, with tangent AD, then as points A and B approach, the angle BAD (subtended by chord and tangent) diminishes without bound and ultimately vanishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: if angle did not vanish one would contain a right angle equal to some circle's subtended angle, contradicting continuity of curvature. Used to justify replacing vanishing arcs by tangents in limit arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma VII — ultimate equality of arcs, chords, and tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: With points coalescing, the ultimate ratio of the arc, chord, and tangent are ratios of equality (the arc, chord, tangent have the same ultimate ratio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Lemma VI: as B→A the small angle vanishes and chords and tangents coincide in ultimate proportion; corollaries: abscissas, chords and arcs can be interchanged in ultimate-ratio arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma VIII — ultimate similarity of triangles formed by chord, tangent, and radius
rubrics_metrics.description: Given chord AB, tangent AD, and straight lines AR, BR to a distant point R, as B→A the ultimate forms of the vanishing triangles (RAB, RACB, RAD) are similar and in the ratio of equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct lines and parallels to transform triangles; as points coalesce angles vanish and finite triangles become coincident in the limit; allows substitution of these limit-triangles in subsequent ultimate-ratio reasonings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma IX — areas of triangles from curve intersections relate in duplicate ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If a given straight line and curve intersect at A and ordinates BD, CE are drawn to that straight line, then as points B,C→A the areas of triangles ABD and ACE are ultimately in the duplicate ratio of sides AD and AE respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs homothetic projections and uses Lemma V on areas; corollary: areas described by velocities are proportional to squares of times when velocities are proportional to times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma X — spaces described under finite force are in duplicate ratio of times
rubrics_metrics.description: Spatia quæ corpus urgente quacunque vi finita describit ... sunt ipso motus initio in duplicata ratione temporum (Spaces described under any finite applied force are, at the very start of motion, in the duplicate ratio of the times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model times by lines, velocities by ordinates, and spaces by areas under ordinates; by Lemma IX areas are in duplicate ratio of times at the motion's outset. Corollaries: errors generated by equal forces applied to similar figure-parts are as square of times; forces are proportional to spaces described at motion's start inversely with square of times, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XI — subtended vanishing angle of contact proportional to duplicate of adjacent arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtensa evanescens anguli contactus ... est ultimo in rationel duplicata subtensæ arcus contermini (The vanishing subtended angle of contact at a point of finite curvature is ultimately in the duplicate ratio of the neighboring subtended arcs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case analysis uses perpendiculars to tangent and circle geometry to relate squares of chords to subtended perpendiculars; corollaries relate squares of chords, sines, sagitta, and areas to tangent subtenses; yields relations used in motion/curvature arguments (e.g., sagitta ~ time^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition I (Section II) — areas swept by radius are proportional to times under centripetal forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas quas corpora in gyros acta radiis ad immobile centrum virium ductis describunt ... esse temporibus proportionales (Areas described by bodies acted upon by radii to a fixed center are contained in planes and are proportional to times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: divide time into equal parts and consider polygonal approximations of the curve where the body moves by straight chords and is impulsively deflected toward the center at each step; triangles formed about the center are equal for equal times; taking limit (sides → 0) gives curved perimeter and area law. Corollaries: (1) velocity toward the center is reciprocally proportional to the perpendicular from center to tangent; (2) forces at points are ultimately proportional to diagonals of constructed parallelograms (relation of impulses to chordal displacements); (3) the converging sagitta/chord relations give measures of centripetal action.
